tasks.short: Draw and evaluate network diagrams and floor plans

steps.what: Submit the floor and device list
Prepare computer-aided network diagrams and floor plans
Evaluate configurations for existing facilities
Check site and floor metadata on the drawing

loop.input: drawing file labels and the site form
loop.output: metadata fields for site id, floor and version
loop.check: Site id, floor and version equal the site form
loop.stop: Leave the field blank and stop if the form has no site id
loop.why_not_simpler: Labels on a drawing are free text and a fixed column map misses them

steps.what: Sign the evaluated drawing version
File the signed drawing with the site

tasks.design: Site id, floor, device list and conduit notes sit on a {WORKFLOW} form. The specialist still prepares the network diagram, floor plan or site configuration and stores the drawing in {DOCS}. A fill may set site id, floor and version on that file, and the specialist checks those metadata fields because a fill can be wrong. The drawing itself is not generated. The specialist signs the evaluated version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Drawings sat in personal files without a site id, so an evaluation could not point at the current floor.
tasks.enabler_now: The site form can carry a site id and a floor, and the drawing file can store those as metadata next to the drawing.
tasks.still_hard: Preparing and evaluating the diagram still takes the specialist's eye. A wrong conduit does not show up as a blank field.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist judges whether the drawing matches the building and what must be redrawn.
tasks.altitude: Filing and metadata take less time. The specialist still draws and still decides that a floor plan is fit to build from.

reach.task: Use the evaluated drawing for a design change
reach.learn: Which floor has a signed drawing and which views are still missing

evidence.claim: Network diagrams and floor plans in a mid-size firm are drawn and checked by a person. The file around the drawing is the part that can be structured.
Digest [S3] says a document product can fill metadata from a prompt, and the vendor warns the fill can be wrong. Use that only for site id, floor and version on the drawing file, not for the diagram.

assumptions: Focal role is the telecommunications specialist. The task ends when an evaluated drawing version is filed. Building from the drawing is a later task.

Input contract: site id, floor, device id, conduit note, drawing version. Producer is the service owner for the site facts, and the specialist for the drawing. A drawing with no site id is not filed as current.
Use the document store's metadata and approval before custom code. The meeting prior covers walkthroughs. The drawing itself is screen work and stays manual.
unknowns: Which drawing tool can store a file that the document store will accept.
Who else may mark a drawing as evaluated.
research_questions: What share of sites has no current drawing with a site id?
How often does an evaluation find a missing floor or conduit view?

already_counted.description: Drawing time stays with the specialist
Evaluation of the floor plan stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Keep the required-view list aligned when a new site type appears

approvals.approved_version: drawing version signed in this evaluation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes drawings stay in personal files, so only the site form is new. The high case assumes metadata is checked quickly but every diagram and every evaluation stays manual. The drawing work is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Sign the telecommunications disaster recovery plan

steps.what: Submit voice routes and recovery times
Maintain failover fields against the inventory

loop.input: route inventory and the target form
loop.output: gap list of missing or conflicting failover sites
loop.check: Each gap names a system id that exists on the inventory
loop.stop: One pass, then the specialist finishes any row with no system id
loop.why_not_simpler: Route names in old plans do not match inventory ids by a fixed rule

steps.what: Draft the telecommunications disaster recovery plan

loop.input: submitted recovery fields and template sections
loop.output: plan draft with each number tagged to a field
loop.check: Every recovery number and failover site equals the submitted field
loop.stop: Leave a blank and stop that section if a number has no field
loop.why_not_simpler: How a voice route fails over is not a fixed sentence

steps.what: Sign the business continuity plan version
File the signed recovery plan
Confirm the next recovery exercise slot

tasks.design: Service owners submit system id, voice route, failover site, recovery-time hours and owner on a {WORKFLOW} form. A template in {DOCS} drafts the disaster recovery plan, and every recovery number must match a submitted field. The specialist signs one version. A later exercise is not part of this task. Incident reports, where the duty applies, stay a separate act.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recovery numbers lived in old plans and mail, so a new draft repeated a failover site that was no longer real.
tasks.enabler_now: The voice-route inventory and the form can share a system id, so each recovery number can be checked against a field.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding how long a voice route may stay down is still a business call, and sector and size decide whether the cyber duty applies.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides which failover is real and which recovery time the business can accept.

ambition.what: Re-sign the recovery plan after a major route change, not only at the yearly review

tasks.altitude: The week moves from rewriting sections to route conflicts and the signature. The specialist can refuse a plan whose numbers do not match the form.

reach.task: Check a design against the signed recovery targets
reach.learn: Which routes have a signed failover site and which rows are still blank

evidence.claim: In a mid-size firm a telecommunications recovery plan is a document plus a review. The hard part is the failover and the recovery time, not the headings.
Digest [S16] and [S17] say Dutch cyber law has been in force since 15 August 2026 and includes a duty of care. Sector and size decide whether a firm is in scope.
Digest [S18] and [S19] say firms in scope have continuity measures and incident reports at 24 hours, 72 hours and one month. Filing those reports is not this task.

assumptions: Focal role is the telecommunications specialist. The task ends when a signed plan version is filed. Running the recovery exercise is a later task.

Input contract: system id, voice route, failover site, recovery-time hours, business owner. Producer is the service owner. If the form is empty the specialist types the same fields from the old plan and marks the row manual.
Use the document store's own templates and approval flow before custom code. The yearly exercise may be a meeting. Writing the plan is document work, and that meeting is not counted here.
unknowns: Whether this firm is in scope of the Dutch cyber duty of care.
Which system is the inventory of voice routes.
Who may sign when the specialist is absent.
research_questions: How often do signed recovery times differ from the last exercise?
Which voice routes have no named owner?

already_counted.description: Specialist edits weak failover sections in the draft
Specialist resolves conflicting recovery times in the sign-off

incremental.description: Update the plan template when a new route type appears
Service owners correct failover sites the form rejects

approvals.approved_version: recovery plan version signed in this review
the same signed recovery plan version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes half the routes still arrive as free text, so the specialist retypes failover sites. The high case assumes the form is used but every plan still has a full sign-off. The recovery exercise and any incident report are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Gather component costs for the system
Total implementation and operation costs
Judge which component costs to include
Sign the cost estimate version
Accept or challenge the signed estimate

tasks.design: Component id, quantity, unit cost, site and cost type land on a {SPREADSHEET} fed by a {WORKFLOW} form. The sheet totals implementation cost and operating cost from those columns. The specialist judges odd rates and missing prices, then signs one estimate version. The table does not raise a purchase.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prices arrived as mail prose and old totals, so a new estimate could not show which unit cost it used.
tasks.enabler_now: A component id and a numeric unit cost can sit on one row, and a total can be a formula on those rows.
tasks.still_hard: A missing price, a one-off discount and the choice of what to include are still the specialist's call.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides which costs belong in the estimate and which price is too odd to use.

ambition.what: Refresh the estimate when a price row changes, instead of rebuilding the whole table

tasks.altitude: Arithmetic leaves the week. The specialist still decides the contents and can refuse an estimate that has a blank price.

reach.task: Accept or challenge the signed cost estimate
reach.learn: Which components have a unit cost and which rows are still blank

evidence.claim: Cost estimates for telecommunications components are a table plus a judgement about what to include. The total itself is arithmetic.
A structured quantity and unit cost can be totalled without a model. Free-text vendor prose still needs a person to type the number.

assumptions: Focal role is the telecommunications specialist. The task ends when a signed estimate version is filed. Raising a purchase is a later task.

Input contract: component id, quantity, unit cost, currency, site, cost type (implementation or operation). Producer is the specialist from vendor prices already in hand. A row with no numeric unit cost is excluded from the total and listed as missing.
Use the spreadsheet's own formulas before custom code. The meeting prior is only the acceptance. Building the table is spreadsheet work.
unknowns: Which currency the estimate must use.
Who supplies the operating cost when the vendor quoted only implementation.
research_questions: What share of estimate rows has no numeric unit cost?
How often does the signed total change after the service owner challenges it?

already_counted.description: Specialist types prices that are not yet numeric
Inclusion judgement stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Add a column when a new cost type appears
Service owners send back challenges on the signed total

approvals.approved_version: cost estimate version signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most prices stay as prose, so the specialist still types every unit cost. The high case assumes clean rows total themselves but every inclusion decision and every sign-off stays manual. The purchase that may follow is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Coordinate installation of hardware and modules

steps.what: Request the hardware or software install
Coordinate installation of modified hardware
Confirm the window on site
Install hardware, software and programming modules
Accept the installation of the modules
File the signed install record

tasks.design: A {WORKFLOW} install order names site, hardware or software module, window and vendor. The specialist coordinates that window. The vendor engineer installs the module in person. The specialist accepts the work only after a check. A live change on the telecommunications system is never unattended, and the order does not install itself.
tasks.previous_blocker: Install dates and module names lived in mail, so two people could arrive for different work.
tasks.enabler_now: An install order can carry a site id, a module id and a window on one record.
tasks.still_hard: The physical install, and the check that the module actually works, still happen on site.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides the window is safe and whether the finished install is acceptable.
tasks.altitude: Chasing dates takes less mail. The specialist still coordinates the site and can refuse an install that was not checked.

reach.task: Install the module in the agreed window
reach.learn: Which module and site the order names, and which window was accepted

evidence.claim: Installing telecommunications hardware and modules is on-site work, often with a vendor. The order and the completion record are the parts that can be structured.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so an unattended change on live telecommunications systems is out of scope.

assumptions: Focal role is the telecommunications specialist. The task ends when the install is accepted or sent back. How the vendor builds the module is out of scope.
Input contract: site id, module id, hardware or software flag, window start, window end, vendor name. Producer is the service owner. An order with no site id or no window is not scheduled.
Use the workflow form and the calendar before custom code. The high in-person prior is accepted: coordination and the install stay on site.
unknowns: Which modules the specialist installs without a vendor.
Whether a change window is frozen outside agreed hours.
research_questions: What share of installs is sent back at the check?
How often does the vendor arrive against a different module id?

already_counted.description: On-site coordination stays with the specialist
Acceptance of the install stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Update the install order fields when a new module type appears
Vendors correct notes that lack a module id

approvals.approved_version: install acceptance signed for this order id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes orders still arrive as mail, so only the form is new and the site work is unchanged. The high case assumes the order is clean but every site visit and every acceptance stays manual. No unattended install is treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Drawing and installation stay in the specialist's hands. The week shifts to signing recovery plans, cost tables and completed installs instead of retyping them.
reach: The network architect receives the signed disaster recovery plan and the evaluated drawing.
The service owner receives the signed cost estimate before a purchase is raised.
skills_to_grow: Mark a drawing as evaluated rather than redrawing it from memory.
Write recovery numbers as fields a template can check.
Separate a unit cost in the table from the judgement about what to include.
role.ambitious_version: Every site has a signed recovery plan, a current cost table and a drawing stored with the site id.
